name: Uterus Didelphys

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Classification of Müllerian Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of two separate uterine bodies each with its own endometrial cavity and two cervices
Confirmation of uterine duplication by imaging modalities such as MRI or 3D ultrasound
Lack of fusion of the Müllerian ducts during embryogenesis leading to two separate uterine horns

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of two separate uterine bodies each with its own endometrial cavity and cervix confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often incidental during evaluation for infertility or recurrent pregnancy loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bicornuate uterine morphology with two distinct endometrial cavities

searchTerms: discomfort during sex due to vaginal wall
problems during pregnancy like preterm birth
pelvic pain not linked to periods
chronic pelvic pain unrelated to cycle

rare.symptomName: Urinary tract anomalies associated with uterine didelphys
searchTerms: urinary tract defects with double uterus
kidney and bladder anomalies with uterine duplication
urinary system malformations linked to uterine didelphys
uterine lining tissue growth due to obstruction
blood accumulation in vagina from blockage

imaging: MRI pelvis showing two separate uterine bodies with distinct endometrial stripes
Hysterosalpingography revealing two separate endometrial cavities
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; developmental anomaly of Müllerian ducts
other: Physical examination may reveal two cervical os or vaginal septum

distinguishingFeatures: Single cervix with two uterine horns fused at the lower segment
Less complete separation of uterine bodies compared to didelphys
Single external uterine contour with internal fibrous or muscular septum
Normal external uterine shape on imaging

redFlags: Pelvic mass or hematocolpos indicating obstructed hemivagina
references: American Society for Reproductive Medicine Classification of Müllerian Anomalies, 2021
Rock JA, et al. Te Linde's Operative Gynecology. 11th Edition. 2015
